open_questions: Do separate key/value pools actually repair choosing, or only the probes? No trained result for premonition/card_pools.py exists anywhere in the audited artifacts (00-evidence.md:43), and under answer-only supplied-card loss the key has no causal path into the answer (00-evidence.md:89).

Is pooling competition necessary at all, or does a cheap fixed contextual mean preserve usable associations? The mean probe rows already decode person/relation/value well (mean->person 1998/2304, mean->value 2304/2304 in the collapsed run, SUMMARY.txt:72) which weakly predicts mean should work — untested end-to-end.

Would the long-read curriculum replicate on seed 1 at 3,745 steps? Only seed 0 has a long run; seed 1 exists only at 1,405 steps, where it scored 27/512 (00-evidence.md:33). Nothing distinguishes 'seed 1 is broken' from 'seed 1 needs longer'.
Is the 4M-vs-28M null real? The 28M run saw 119.37M nominal tokens vs 395.67M for 4M (00-evidence.md:63), so capacity and exposure are fully confounded.

Are the artifacts/premonition-1h-4090-run_*.log runs on the RTX 4090 the filename claims, or on Ben's own RTX 5070 Ti? Hardware provenance is unlabelled inside the logs, which matters for reusing their throughput numbers as 5070 Ti budgets.

Which tokenizer is canonical? All three BensPC pilots used premonition-tok-v2.json with 7,289 IDs, while premonition/identity.py requires premonition-tok-v2-fallback.json with 7,068 IDs (00-evidence.md:61). Until this is reconciled no pilot checkpoint can be admitted for an official verdict.

Can any held-out score still be used as primary evidence? Held-out numbers combine validation and test, and test was consulted during the iterative pilot (00-evidence.md:65). Fresh test identities are needed.
Does anything in the project retain skills over time? No retention or continued-learning result exists in any artifact (00-evidence.md:49), yet lifelong learning is the project's headline claim.

How much of the 23.4% held-out Core score is leakage rather than reading? All three saved gates report leak_detectors: FAIL including not-told, person and yes/no cues (00-evidence.md:65), so the true label-free ceiling is unknown.

Does the ~1/3 choosing score exceed any shortcut at all? Measured simple shortcuts reach 53.71% one-hop / 53.42% two-hop on validation (00-evidence.md:27), above every choosing score recorded — so choosing may currently be worse than not reasoning.

strengths.what: ESTABLISHED. Reading one supplied fact card is fully repaired, on the untouched test, on two seeds, by two independent fixes. Original D scored 112/1024 and 111/1024 (wilson95 [0.0917,0.130] and [0.0908,0.1289], chance 6.25%); D-card-bypass and D-think-gated each scored 1024/1024 (wilson95 [0.9963,1.0]) at seeds 0 and 1. Four-for-four across fixes and seeds makes this the most trustworthy result in the project.

ESTABLISHED. The failure was causally localised to the Think block, not to the reader or the card writer. With no Think pass the writer-card arm reaches 477/512 val (93.2%) and 956/1024 probe-scored; inserting one Think pass drops the identical setup to 55/512 val (10.7%) and 113/1024. Collapse anatomy matches: cos_post(median) 0.9756 with Think vs 0.2362 without, and attention on the card row 0.0774 vs 0.3291 (uniform = 0.0674).

ESTABLISHED. The repaired copying arms are causally well-behaved, not pattern-matching: on 256 paired fresh visits each, irrelevant fact changes left the answer unchanged 256/256 with both members correct, and relevant changes flipped the answer with both correct 256/256; swap-follows 1024/1024 (original 0). Original D managed relevant both-correct 1/256.

ESTABLISHED. On the harder toy ladder, gold-only reading is perfect on the untouched test for every repaired arm: one-hop 512/512, practised two-hop 323/323, held-out two-hop 189/189. Reading supplied evidence is therefore not the bottleneck anywhere.

ESTABLISHED. The card store is load-bearing, verified by two independent ablations. D-noask (reader only, no cards) stayed at chance: 42/512 val (8.2%) on the m02 toy and 41/512 / 27/341 / 8/171 on the ladder after 3,750 steps; nothink-noask scored 40/512 one-hop on test. Removing cards from a trained bypass model drops it to 34/512 one-hop.

PLAUSIBLE, ONE SEED. Own retrieval plus reading works end-to-end for one-hop and practised two-hop, given a long gold-reading curriculum and 3,745 steps: test one-hop 356/512 (69.5%, all needed cards fetched 350/512) and practised two-hop 154/323 (47.7%). The same architecture on the default curriculum reached only 32/512. Single seed, and the seed-1 replication at 1,405 steps failed.

ESTABLISHED (mechanism). The information loss happens at pooling, not at reading. Reader states at the person and value token positions decode perfectly (person_tok->person 2304/2304, value_tok->value 2304/2304) in every checkpoint, while pooled card vectors keep only one field: the answer-only run puts 97.9% of pool mass on the value token with pooled->person 131/2304, whereas the retrieval-trained seed-0 run puts 71.0% on relation with pooled->value 149/2304. Reproduced across six checkpoints.

ESTABLISHED (Core track). The one-visit-per-row 2048-token window is a real improvement over random 768-token cuts, on matched 600 s runs: final loss 0.734 -> 0.656, train held-in 382/991 (38.55%) -> 475/991 (47.93%), held-out visible 677/3782 (17.90%) -> 881/3763 (23.41%), and 'not told' answers 22/579 -> 169/571. Confounded by a parameter change (5,222,144 -> 5,549,824) and by exposure, so the size of the effect is uncertain even though its direction is consistent.

ESTABLISHED (infrastructure). Evaluation trustworthiness measurably improved: contender A showed at least one earlier answer in 7,675/8,675 inputs (88.5%, 34,801 leaked answers) and now shows 0 with all 8,675 passing an automatic audit; contender C's retrieval blind spot affected 62% of inputs and hid a needed fact in 413 questions, and the repaired search now finds 231 of 464. Scoring fails closed on tokenizer/vocab/shape mismatch, and all 49 frozen-source and 78 artifact hashes re-verified read-only.

ESTABLISHED. The data pipeline is not the limiter on the 5070 Ti: world_bottleneck stall was 0.2-0.9% on the three 19 Sep pilots, and the forgetting-baseline probe recorded its 7 evaluation points in every run. Cost is small and measured: whole overnight ledger 3,478.2 s (58.0 min) of local Mac CPU, $0.00 rental against the $30 cap.

maps.summary: Two evidence bodies exist. The Premonition-mini toy ladder (local Mac CPU, ~58 min total, $0 rental) has firmly established that reading one supplied fact card works (1024/1024 test, two fixes, two seeds) and that the earlier failure came from the Think block collapsing rows; probes locate the remaining loss precisely at card pooling, where a single vector keeps either identity or value but not both. Everything downstream is still broken: choosing among distractor cards sits at 32-36%, below a measured 53.7% shortcut; held-out two-hop composition is 14/189; the second fetch requests the wrong relation. The Core transformer track (RTX 5070 Ti, 600 s runs) reached 23.4% held-out against a 90% gate, with leak detectors failing and fresh-name accuracy at 0.0%.

Premonition-mini "D" (~2.01M params, d=128) reads a whole visit with a 3-layer reader [minGRU, block-local attention W=64 RoPE, minGRU], writes one card per non-question line by attention-pooling that line's reader states into a unit key (64) and a value (128), then, at each question's "[answer]" token, runs a Think tensor of 76 rows (40 question states, 16 entity slots, 16 card rows, 4 registers) through one shared 2-layer bidirectional transformer block looped up to 8 times. Register 0 drives ASK (cosine query x card keys, scaled by learned kappa plus age bias, top-4) and HALT. Fetched cards enter as value + age embedding + row-type embedding; a binder gates each mentioned entity slot. A one-block decoder cross-attends the think rows and emits answer tokens through the tied embedding, with ENT ids restricted to entities actually mentioned.

strengths.what: Causal privilege is enforced structurally, not by convention: a question sees only cards on lines strictly before its own, wipes add a floor, and evidence lines with no eligible card are counted rather than silently dropped.
ASK is trained with a set cross-entropy over the still-unfetched gold cards, so retrieval supervision needs no hop order and degrades gracefully as cards accumulate.
strengths.evidence: premonition/store.py:33-35; model.py:596-601 (`need = gold & ~fetched`), spec design/06-premonition-mini-spec.md L_ask row of the loss table

strengths.what: Name handling is rule-based and hard-constrained: entity ids are the only way to name a person, and generation of an unmentioned ENT id is masked to -inf, so a fresh name is copied exactly and can never be hallucinated.
strengths.evidence: premonition/model.py:395-407 (_mentions), model.py:738-740 and 747 (banned mask), design/06-premonition-mini-spec.md §2 "Names as pointers"

strengths.what: Deep supervision: the decoder loss and a HALT target are computed at every loop, not only the last, with a 0.2 down-weight before all gold cards are in. This matches the TRM/HRM finding that deep supervision, not the recursion itself, carries most of the gain.
strengths.evidence: premonition/model.py:570-588 (ans_terms, halt_terms, `scale = where(have_all, 1.0, early_ans)`); config.py:53 `early_ans = 0.2`; design/research/2026-09-19-overnight-research-note.md TRM entry

strengths.what: Compute accounting is real and falsifiable: FLOPs are measured with FlopCounterMode, fitted to a*tokens + b*question_loops with a reported worst relative residual, and cross-checked against a hand count in the same convention.
strengths.evidence: premonition/flops.py:97-136 (measure_mini, fit_flops), flops.py:139-169 (mini_hand_count); spec §4 requires agreement within 15%

strengths.what: Variant discipline is unusually clean for A/B causality: diagnostic variants copy every shared weight from the baseline and verify the state-dict delta is exactly the new parameter, and the new card writer is built inside fork_rng so the global RNG stream is bit-identical to the baseline's.
minGRU forget gates are initialised so memory time constants are spread log-uniformly over 2..512 tokens, giving the recurrence a usable range of horizons at step 0 instead of one default decay.
strengths.evidence: premonition/model.py:360-364 (`tau = logspace(log10(2), log10(512), d)`; bias = logit(1/tau))

strengths.what: Matched-context evaluation against the transformer baselines is built in: W-full re-crops each question's row to A's 768-token window and re-reads it with a fresh reader state; W-store keeps the recurrence but drops the cards.
strengths.evidence: premonition/model.py:671-695 and crop_to_windows at model.py:760-802; spec §2 "Wipes"

strengths.what: The config computes the parameter breakdown by hand and refuses to construct a d=128 model outside the 1.9-2.15M band, so the compute-matching claim cannot silently drift.

weaknesses.what: A card's retrieval key and its content value are both linear projections of ONE pooled vector produced by ONE scalar score per token, so addressing and reading compete for the same softmax. The card physically cannot hold both "whose relation this is" and "what it says".
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/model.py:171-197 (single `self.pool = nn.Linear(d, 1)`, `CardStore.write(self.key(pooled), self.value(pooled), ...)`); measured 0.979 attention mass on the value token and person decodable in 116/2048 probes (design/research/final-sweep-2026-09-19/README.md evidence table; premonition/card_pools.py:5-10)

weaknesses.what: A fetched card re-enters Think as value + age embedding + row-type embedding only. Its key, source tag, line index, diary pointer and entity ids are all written into the store but never given to the model, so once the pooled value has collapsed there is no other handle on card identity.

weaknesses.suspected_cause: The row format was designed assuming the pooled value would be self-describing; combined with the pooling collapse it leaves the decoder nothing to choose with (supplied-card choosing 166-182/512).

weaknesses.what: The decoder's first cross-attention query is question-blind: decoding starts from the single "[answer]" token, which is the same token for every question, so the first read of the think rows cannot be conditioned on what was asked unless Think already marked the right row.
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/model.py:560-561 (`start_token = tokens[q_visit, q_span[:,1]-1]`) and model.py:741 (`sequence = ...unsqueeze(1)`); diagnosis and the +qread remedy at premonition/ovn_qread.py:3-9
weaknesses.suspected_cause: Encoder-decoder split where the question is only an encoder input; the fix costs no parameters (PREFIX=6 extra decoder positions, ovn_qread.py:22) but is still a diagnostic subclass, not baseline D.

weaknesses.what: Think returns its residual stream unnormalised and adds the loop-step embedding to EVERY row before each pass, which lets a loop add one shared vector to all 76 rows. Measured: a row-shared update of norm ~8.7 with only ~0.3 row-to-row spread, and Think gates that trained nearly closed.
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/model.py:236-240 (`x = x + self.step.weight[step]`, no output norm) vs the reader which does end in a LayerNorm (model.py:163,168); measured shortcut quoted in premonition/ovn_variants.py:8-10; "Think gates nearly closed" in design/research/final-sweep-2026-09-19/README.md

weaknesses.what: Residual initialisation is scaled for a 6-branch network (3 reader layers + 2 think layers + 1 decoder) but the think block is executed up to 8 times, so the true inference-time depth is 3 + 2x8 + 1 = 20 branches and the looped block is under-damped by roughly a factor of 1.8 in std.

weaknesses.suspected_cause: Depth counted from module count rather than from unrolled compute; plausibly a direct contributor to the residual-drift and gate-closing above.

weaknesses.what: Card-row eviction is silently unrecoverable. Rows are overwritten modulo 16, but `fetched` is never cleared and `eligible` permanently excludes any fetched card, so an evicted card can never be re-fetched and its value is simply gone for the rest of the episode.

weaknesses.suspected_cause: FIFO ring buffer plus a monotone "already fetched" mask designed independently; nothing reconciles them.

weaknesses.what: Parameter allocation is inverted relative to the diagnosed bottleneck: 40.6% of the model is the token embedding and the card writer, the module every diagnostic blames, gets 1.2%.
weaknesses.evidence: design/06-premonition-mini-spec.md §1 table: embedding 817,664; card writer 25,089; think 466,448; decoder 199,040; reader 496,384; total 2,013,140 (matches config.py:129-153)
weaknesses.suspected_cause: A 6,388-id tied vocabulary at d=128 in a 2M budget; the writer was sized as a projection rather than as an encoder of a line into a structured record.

weaknesses.what: The slot binder (65,792 params, 2.6x the card writer) runs as a Python loop over fetch slots using non-accumulating index_put, and is explicitly excluded from the FLOP hand count as "< 1%".
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/model.py:471-481 (`for k in range(cards.shape[1])`, `episode.x.index_put(...)` without accumulate); premonition/flops.py:144 ("Leaves out the slot binder"); spec §1 lists the binder at 65,792

weaknesses.what: The recurrent memory is sign-constrained: the log-space scan makes h_t strictly positive, so the reader's state can only accumulate and decay, never cancel. Erasure is available only through the (1 - z) factor. Combined with exactly ONE local-attention layer of window 64, all long-range binding inside a visit passes through a positive accumulator.
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/model.py:46-48 (`_log_g`: g(x) = x+0.5 or sigmoid(x), always > 0), model.py:51-70 (scan is computed in log space and exponentiated), config.py:27 `reader = ("gru", "attn", "gru")`, config.py:29 `window = 64`
weaknesses.suspected_cause: The log-space parallel scan requires positive candidates; expressivity was traded for scan stability. A line's card is pooled from these states, so identity that must survive from an earlier line arrives through this channel.

weaknesses.what: The equal-FLOPs comparison against A/B/C systematically undercounts D. FlopCounterMode counts only matmuls and attention, and the minGRU scan (a chunked fp32 Python loop producing [B, T, d] fp32 intermediates per layer, twice) is pure elementwise work.

weaknesses.suspected_cause: A FLOP convention chosen for transformer comparability applied to a non-transformer; the secondary wall-clock check exists but is explicitly "not a kill".

weaknesses.what: HALT is trained on teacher-forced correctness but used on free-running greedy decoding, and at weight 0.1. The target is "every answer token argmax-correct given the GOLD prefix", which is a strictly easier event than the greedy rollout being right.
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/model.py:561 (`inputs` are gold-shifted), model.py:579-588 (`wrong` from argmax against gold, `correct` becomes the BCE target), vs model.py:745-756 (greedy feeds its own tokens); config.py:51 `w_halt = 0.1`
weaknesses.suspected_cause: Deep-supervision loss reused as a stopping signal without an exposure-bias correction.

weaknesses.what: Think rewrites the card rows in place at every loop, so evidence is not read-only; the only clean evidence path (D-card-bypass) exists solely as a diagnostic subclass and is not the baseline.
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/model.py:486-487 (`rows = self.think(...); episode.x = episode.x.index_copy(0, index, rows)`); premonition/answer_path.py:10-13 and 114-121 (CardBypassMini keeps the pre-Think rows for the decoder); "the thinking scratchpad damages facts it is allowed to rewrite" in design/research/2026-09-19-overnight-research-note.md

weaknesses.what: There is no regularisation of any kind in the reasoner: no dropout, no stochastic depth, no noise, and no auxiliary diversity term. Reported seed spread on the same setting is 503/512 vs 27/512.
weaknesses.evidence: grep of premonition/model.py finds no Dropout module (modules are LayerNorm, Linear, Embedding, Mlp, GELU only, model.py:78-291); seed instability recorded in design/research/final-sweep-2026-09-19/README.md and the overnight note's ladder table (seed 1 at 1500 steps finds 390/512 but reads 27/512)

maps.summary: Premonition-mini's knowledge store is an episode-scoped card store rebuilt from the input like a KV cache (premonition/store.py:1-12). The reader emits one card per non-question line: a softmax-pooled line vector projected to a unit key (64d) and a value (128d), plus tags, entity ids and a diary pointer (model.py:171-197, store.py:38-70). At each think loop, register 0 produces one query; scores are kappa*q.k + learned age bias over all eligible earlier cards plus a learned NULL (store.py:106-117). Hard top-4 selection inserts card values as think rows (FIFO, 16 rows) and binds them into 16 entity slots (model.py:446-481). Retrieval is supervised only by an oracle set cross-entropy over evidence lines (model.py:596-601). Names become ENT ids by a rule-based detector (pointer.py:63-102). Contender C instead does BM25 line recall into a 768-token window (lookup.py).

strengths.what: Store holds no trained weights and is rebuilt from the visit like a KV cache, so evaluation cannot write memory; this makes "no card writes while testing" true by construction and keeps the 2M parameter count honest
strengths.evidence: premonition/store.py:1-12; design/06-premonition-mini-spec.md "Decided: it is rebuilt from the input like a KV cache" (§2 Scope)

strengths.what: Eligibility is strictly causal and composable: a question sees only cards on lines < its own line, optionally above a wipe floor, with NULL always eligible and already-fetched cards excluded; wipes are a cheap view (dataclasses.replace) rather than a rebuild
Wipe machinery gives a real apples-to-apples control against A's 768-token window: W-store drops cards/names but keeps the reader state, W-full re-crops the batch and re-reads
The gold-evidence mapper is defensive: it distinguishes "never told" (target = NULL) from evidence lines that map to no eligible card, and returns a `missing` counter that the tests assert stays zero
FIFO eviction risk is measured rather than assumed: card_stats counts questions that overflowed the 16 card rows and, of those, how many lost a gold card
The pointerizer is exactly invertible: detokenise(pointerize(text)) reproduces the tokenizer-normalised text with every name in its original spelling, so a fresh name is copied, never generated
strengths.evidence: premonition/pointer.py:214-238 (detokenise/restored); premonition/model.py:741-743 bans entity ids not mentioned in the visible prefix

strengths.what: Label leakage through names is closed off at the preprocessing layer: entity ids bind over visible text only, a target name the visible prefix never mentioned stays plain tokens and is flagged (`unbound`), and names appearing only in answers/feedback are reported (`label_only_names`)

Everything that could silently change meaning is digest-pinned and fails closed: preprocessing spec digest, BM25 table sha256, name-detector digest, tokenizer digest, and a verdict guard that refuses mixed regimes or non-primary reports

Entity numbering is randomised per visit at batch time from an identity-numbered cache, so the same cached visit yields different ENT permutations across epochs without rebuilding the cache — a cheap defence against memorising ENT ids

C's lookup closes the window/candidate gap by construction: it iterates the recall boundary until C's own window starts exactly at the boundary, and asserts no line is both recalled and windowed and that no line falls between them
strengths.evidence: premonition/lookup.py:396-414; gap_lines reported and 0 under the current rule (lookup.py:345-349, 426-453)

maps.summary: Two trainers share one base. `learnlab/train.py` is an AdamW streaming LM trainer (matrices decayed, biases/norms not; linear warmup then CONSTANT lr; grad clip 1.0; bf16 autocast only on CUDA; fused Adam only on CUDA; 14 GiB memory guard; dead-GELU/grad-norm/weight-norm logging). Core (step1) feeds it one whole visit per 2048-token row, padded with <eos> and loss-masked; 4M/lr 1e-3, 28M/6e-4, ~600 s runs on the 5070 Ti. `premonition/train.py` subclasses it as `MiniTrainer`: whole-visit `VisitBatch`es, a FLOP budget instead of a step count, and a 3-phase curriculum (gold 0-5%, teacher 5-30%, own 30-100% with p_own ramping to 0.75). Four losses (L_lm, L_ask = BCE + set-CE, L_ans deep-supervised at every loop, L_halt) with weights 1.0/0.5/1.0/0.1 and `early_ans` 0.2. The overnight ladder/retrieval scripts run all of this on CPU.

strengths.what: FLOP-budget training with a measured, fitted cost model (FLOPs = a*padded_tokens + b*sum(questions x loops), FlopCounterMode-calibrated), so every contender is compared at equal compute and the run reports budget_ok within tolerance
strengths.evidence: premonition/train.py:259-283 (calibrate/batch_cost), premonition/train.py:436-449 (budget_ok, fit, loop_mismatches); artifacts/opus-ovn-20260918-235851/SUMMARY.txt:79-98 all arms stop='flop budget'

strengths.what: Every evaluation runs inside `read_only`, which digests model, optimizer and RNG state and raises ReadOnlyViolation if scoring mutated anything - no silent train/eval leakage

Unusually rich in-training instrumentation: gold recall@4 vs a random-fetch baseline, FIFO card overflow and gold-eviction counts, share of answer terms still at the early 0.2 weight, questions that never reach full weight, dead-GELU fraction, grad norm, weight norm, halt rate, loops/question, tokens/s
Windows GPU-spill memory guard aborts the run instead of silently dropping to ~1/30 speed; checked after step 1 and every 50 steps

Length-bucketed dynamic batching for Premonition (visits x longest visit <= max_tokens, shuffled within pools, batches reshuffled each epoch) plus a fresh random entity permutation per visit per epoch - real anti-memorisation pressure on names
The visit-aligned window fix in the Core track is a clean, measured win: one visit per 2048-token row starting with <eos> like an eval prompt, only 8 of 162,049 visits truncated
strengths.evidence: learnlab/step1.py:1143-1157 (_aligned); design/06-step1-pilot-results.md table: loss 0.734 -> 0.656, held-out 17.9% -> 23.4%, train-split 36% -> 44%

strengths.what: Strong experiment hygiene in the overnight scripts: validation used for development, test scored once behind a guard, Wilson 95% intervals on every cell, a wall-second ledger with a hard cap, checkpoint sha256 and an arm-identity block
The training stream is deterministic and digest-verified batch by batch, so a run can be replayed and two arms provably saw identical data
The gold-card warm-up demonstrably works when it is long enough: 600 gold-only steps out of 2000 took supplied-card one-hop reading from 264/512 to 512/512, and every top arm uses it
Optimizer hygiene is correct and cheap: weight decay only on dim>=2 tensors, grad clipping with the norm still logged when clipping is off, per-step finite-gradient check that stops the run

weaknesses.what: The RTX 5070 Ti is unused by every Premonition run - device is hardcoded to CPU, and autocast/fused-AdamW are gated on CUDA so even an MPS run is fp32
weaknesses.evidence: scripts/premonition_ovn_retrieval.py:167-168 MiniTrainer(..., "cpu", ...); premonition/train.py:1012 train_toy(..., "cpu", ...); premonition/train.py:307 autocast(enabled=self.device.type == "cuda"); learnlab/train.py:87 fused=True if cuda else None; SUMMARY.txt:79-98 train_s=181-490 s per arm under a 1800 s CPU ledger
weaknesses.suspected_cause: The overnight scripts were written under a 30-minute CPU ledger and never parameterised for device; train_d takes device= but the toy/ladder/retrieval entry points do not. Every conclusion about seeds, gates and curricula rests on 1405-4000-step CPU runs that the local GPU could run 10-50x longer.

weaknesses.what: The Think gate alpha is initialised at exactly 0 and multiplies the WHOLE update, so at step 0 the Think block's own weights receive exactly zero gradient - a self-reinforcing dead branch, not evidence that recurrence is useless
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/answer_path.py:56-59 `self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(()))`, `return x + self.alpha * (super().forward(x, valid, step) - x)`; measured alpha after 2000 steps: 0.01809 and 0.04196 in artifacts/opus-ovn-20260918-235851/SUMMARY.txt:21,25
weaknesses.suspected_cause: d(Think params) is proportional to alpha, and d(alpha) depends on a randomly-initialised Think output being useful. Standard fixes (init alpha small-but-nonzero, e.g. 0.1; or gate only the residual delta while keeping an ungated warm-up phase) were never tried.

weaknesses.what: Deep supervision decodes the SAME answer target from EVERY think loop through the SAME decoder and averages, so the optimum is an answer already decodable at loop 1 - there is no gradient pressure for a loop to do anything new
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/model.py:568-586 (per-loop _decode_logits + CE) and :617 `l_ans = torch.cat(ans_terms).sum() / pairs`; the decode-last-row-only ablation changed almost nothing (choose:one_hop 181/512 vs 174/512, SUMMARY.txt:21,25)
weaknesses.suspected_cause: Deep supervision was chosen for trainability. Combined with the near-zero alpha it removes both the pressure and the path for recurrence. The '+final' control is weak evidence precisely because the gates were already shut.

weaknesses.what: HALT is trained as 'is my answer exactly correct right now' but never actually used during training - loop counts are fixed by mode (2 / ceil(|G|/4)+3 / 8), while at evaluation `answer()` halts on its own policy
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/model.py:588 BCE(halt, correct); premonition/train.py:107-118 planned_loops; premonition/model.py:716-724 (answer halts when sigmoid(halt) > 0.5)
weaknesses.suspected_cause: Classic exposure bias. Early in training nothing is correct so the target is ~0 everywhere; once loop-1 answers are right the target is 1 at every loop, i.e. halt immediately. The head never learns 'another loop would help'.

weaknesses.what: There is no learning-rate decay anywhere - warmup then a constant LR for the whole run, in both tracks
weaknesses.evidence: learnlab/train.py:100-102 `lr_at` returns lr * min(1,(step+1)/warmup); premonition/train.py:120-126 mini_train_config(lr=1e-3, warmup_steps=100); learnlab/step1.py:103 DEFAULT_LR 4M=1e-3
weaknesses.suspected_cause: Simplicity. A constant 1e-3 for 10,128 steps (Core) or thousands of tiny-batch steps (Premonition) keeps the model in a high-noise regime to the last step, which both inflates final-loss/accuracy variance and is a strong candidate for the seed split.

weaknesses.what: Seed instability is measured but not managed: one seed per arm, no best-on-validation checkpoint selection, no early stopping, no restarts, no median-of-seeds reporting. The failing seed sits at chance
weaknesses.evidence: SUMMARY.txt:84 gold_read one_hop=503/512 (seed 0) vs :96 27/512 (seed 1) at the same 1405 steps; chance is 1/16 = 32/512. premonition/train.py:1086-1092 train_d saves only the final model; learnlab/step1.py:2309-2313 step1 saves once at the end
weaknesses.suspected_cause: Checkpointing is end-of-run only, so a run that learns then collapses is unrecoverable and an unlucky seed is simply lost. With eval_every already producing validation numbers, keeping the best checkpoint is nearly free.

weaknesses.what: The shipped default gold phase is 5% of the budget, while every run that actually learned used 30% - the known-bad default is still the one train_d uses
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/train.py:85-88 `gold_until: float = 0.05`; SUMMARY.txt:79-98 every successful arm overrides to {"gold_until": 0.3, "teacher_until": 0.55, "ramp_until": 0.8}; the D-default arm scored gold_read one_hop=32/512 (SUMMARY.txt:88) vs 503/512 for longread
weaknesses.suspected_cause: The 5/30/60 split came from the design doc (06 section 3) as an assumption 'tuned in build step 5' and was never updated after the longread evidence.

weaknesses.what: Stopping on FLOPs rather than steps makes arms step-mismatched and makes the curriculum phase boundaries depend on the cost-fit residual
weaknesses.evidence: SUMMARY.txt:79-98 steps=1405, 1517, 3745, 3750 across arms nominally asking for 1500/4000; premonition/train.py:271-275 (curriculum keyed on self.flops/self.flop_budget), :420 loop_mismatches counted
weaknesses.suspected_cause: FLOP parity is the right fairness axis for the final verdict, but during development it confounds 'this arm is better' with 'this arm got 1405 steps and that one got 3745'. No step-matched control run exists.

weaknesses.what: L_ask adds two unnormalised means (per-loop ASK BCE + set cross-entropy) under one weight of 0.5, and the set CE is satisfied by ONE gold card landing in the top-4 - so the second hop's fetch is effectively unsupervised
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/model.py:596-601, :619-622 `l_ask = mean(bce); l_ask = l_ask + mean(set_terms)`; premonition/config.py:46 w_ask=0.5; the risk is stated in premonition/train.py:31-33; outcome: second-fetch relation correct 0/171 (default) and 9/171 (longread), design/research/final-sweep-2026-09-19/README.md evidence table
weaknesses.suspected_cause: set_cross_entropy over G\F rewards any single member. Multi-gold questions need either a per-member term or a top-k coverage loss; the existing `multi_gold_full_fetched` diagnostic already exposes the gap but no loss term targets it.

weaknesses.what: The whole exp1 ladder - the experiment that produced the 166-182/512 'choosing' number - trains ONLY answer cross-entropy. No L_lm, no L_ask, no L_halt, and the cards are supplied, so 'which card is right' has no direct supervision at all
weaknesses.evidence: scripts/premonition_ovn_ladder.py:316-337 `loss_of` returns only mean CE over decoded rows; :457 the only loss called in cmd_train; SUMMARY.txt:6-45 choose:one_hop 141-171/512 across every arm
weaknesses.suspected_cause: The ladder was designed to isolate the answer path, but the conclusion drawn from it ('choosing is weak') is partly a statement about a training signal that was deliberately removed. A card-selection auxiliary loss on this same toy is a cheap, decisive control.

weaknesses.what: Answer tokens are ~1-2% of the Core track's LM tokens and `lm_loss` weights every target identically; there is no per-token weighting hook
weaknesses.evidence: learnlab/core.py:110-122 (uniform mean CE, mask is boolean only); design/06-step1-pilot-results.md 'Answer tokens are about 1-2% of all tokens' listed as a cause of slow learning, with the mitigation still an open decision for Ben
weaknesses.suspected_cause: The loss mask is boolean, so upweighting answers would need a float weight. The diagnosis has been written down twice without a code change.

weaknesses.what: About 40% of the Core track's GPU time is spent on <eos> padding: visits average ~1,160 tokens but every row is padded to 2048, with no packing and no variable-length batching
weaknesses.evidence: learnlab/step1.py:1150-1156 (pad to `length` with eos, mask False); design/06-step1-pilot-results.md '332M (~200M real)' for run 20260919T092801Z; artifacts/.../premonition-step1-4M-1789810658957235700-16832.json train.tokens = 331,874,304
weaknesses.suspected_cause: Alignment was implemented as pad-to-fixed-length because Trainer._next_batch concatenates and unfolds a flat token stream. Packing two short visits per row (with a segment-reset mask) would recover most of that 40%.

weaknesses.what: The GPU is under-used and the 28M comparison was compute-starved, so '28M no better than 4M' is not an architecture finding
weaknesses.evidence: artifacts/.../premonition-step1-4M-...json peak_gpu_reserved_bytes = 5,687,476,224 (5.3 GiB of a 16 GB card, against a 14 GiB limit); 4M ran at 751k tok/s for 396M tokens vs 28M at 224k tok/s for 119M tokens (design/06-step1-pilot-results.md table) - roughly 16 epochs vs 5 over a 24.15M-token train set
weaknesses.suspected_cause: Batch 32 x 2048 was kept fixed across sizes and the run length was fixed at 600 s rather than at token parity. The final-sweep README already flags this ('The larger model received much less exposure').

weaknesses.what: The model is never trained on the retrieval distribution it is evaluated under: p_own caps at 0.75, teacher cards are RANDOM members of G\F plus distractors, and the gold phase preloads perfect evidence
weaknesses.evidence: premonition/train.py:88 p_own_max=0.75; premonition/model.py:630-640 _teacher_cards (random draw from need); measured gap in one checkpoint: fixed_K4 own-retrieval one_hop=124/512 vs gold_read_K2 one_hop=503/512 (SUMMARY.txt:82-84)
weaknesses.suspected_cause: Scheduled sampling that never reaches 1.0. The model's own query head only ever sees registers built in a world where correct cards arrive for free, so its errors are never in-distribution during training.

weaknesses.what: No dropout, label smoothing, or any regulariser anywhere, while the Core track does roughly 8-16 passes over a 24.15M-token corpus with a 4M-parameter model
weaknesses.evidence: grep for Dropout/label_smoothing across learnlab/*.py and premonition/*.py returns zero hits; artifacts/.../premonition-step1-4M-...json data.train_tokens = 24,150,067 vs train.tokens = 331,874,304; design/06-step1-pilot-results.md train-split 44% vs held-out 23.4%
weaknesses.suspected_cause: A near-2x train/held-out gap on a 4M model at 8+ epochs with constant LR is consistent with memorisation; the entity-permutation trick exists for Premonition batches but has no Core-track counterpart.

maps.summary: Village v0 is a deterministic 6x6-10x10 grid world (40 places, ~60 object kinds, 5-12 Zipf-bursty made-up names, 1-3 rules from R1-R9) simulated in learnlab/village/, rendered through a Qwen-written sentence-pattern bank (learnlab/patterns.py, data/village/patterns/bank-v1.json), tokenized by a byte-BPE with syllable-splitting for names, and graded by a state-tracking oracle over 13 question types plus counterfactual twins. learnlab/splits.py hash-splits four axes (name, template, teacher_style, rule_family) into a checked manifest; learnlab/leaks.py runs 10 dumb guessers per answer class against matched nulls; learnlab/readonly.py fingerprints the model during eval. Generation is fast (20,000 train visits in 74 s) and eval is cheap (5.5 s), but the question-phrasing bank is starved and the training corpus is small enough to be reused 13.7 times.

strengths.what: World generation and evaluation are both extremely cheap, so data experiments are nearly free. 20,000 train visits (236 MB, 171,701 questions) generate in 74.2 s; validation/test 600 visits each in ~6.3 s; oracle indexing 4.1-6.7 s per split; the whole final evaluation of 3,827 held-out + 991 train-split + 1,000 long-range + 428 pair items takes 5.46 s on the 5070 Ti.

The name tokenizer genuinely removes the memorise-the-name shortcut. Names are built from 24 two-letter syllables and any all-syllable word is split into syllables before BPE, so held-out names cost the same tokens as train names: 0/2,748 train, 0/937 validation and 0/929 test names are single tokens, and the mean-pieces gap across splits is 0.0026.
strengths.evidence: learnlab/tokenizer.py:231-246 (_split); same artifact, name_token_audit (single_token=0 everywhere, max_mean_gap=0.00256, warning=null)

strengths.what: The leak panel is real, statistically disciplined, and currently catching things. Ten detectors per answer class (majority, bag-of-words, bigram, question-only, metadata, position, most-mentioned, last-mention, target-line) are each compared with their own matched null by an exact one-sided binomial test at alpha=0.01 with a 0.05 effect margin and a 100-item floor; it reports 8 leaking detectors across 3 classes rather than a clean pass.
strengths.evidence: learnlab/leaks.py:1-13, learnlab/policy.py ALPHA=0.01/LEAK_MARGIN=0.05/LEAK_MIN_ITEMS=100; artifact leaks.leaking_detectors (person/target_line 38.0% vs null 18.3%, p_adj=1.7e-11)

strengths.what: The split machinery is independently auditable rather than trust-based: a hash manifest with a 64-item canary per axis, manifest_differences() that names exactly what changed, and splits.audit_examples() which re-scans the generated text for foreign-split vocabulary and for own-split names the provenance never recorded, raising SplitLeak on any hit.

read_only evaluation is unusually thorough: parameter/buffer identity, dtype, stride, storage pointer, version counter, content digest, .grad, module tree, optimizer state_dict and RNG state (python/numpy/torch/CUDA/MPS) are all snapshotted and verified on exit, with the .data blind spot documented.

Slice tagging for Experiment 1 is already the right shape for honest comparisons: near/far defined by the contender's real 736-token cut, multi-hop by depth 2-5, changed/stale by replaying the visit and re-asking the oracle after every earlier step, fresh-vs-seen names, reworded, and an explicit exclusion list that keeps the leak-flagged classes (q.who_has, q.in_container) and in-visit repeats out of every decision cell.

The oracle grades plans by acting them out rather than by string match, so any working plan counts, and the run records the checker used and how many were checked (549/549 plan questions oracle-checked, with right_exact and right_other_working_plan reported separately).
strengths.evidence: artifact final.plan_grading {checker: learnlab.village.oracle.check_plan, plan_questions: 549, checked_by_oracle: 549}; learnlab/village/oracle.py:19

strengths.what: Input hygiene is audited per eval set: answers already present in the input, questions asked earlier with a different answer, and oracle-checked plans are counted, and the 64 held-out questions already answered identically earlier in their own input are reported apart and excluded from the gate.

The world semantics are tight enough for an exact oracle: every rule firing is deterministic, timed rules within a village have distinct times so ordering never matters, (colour, kind) stays unique for the village's life so a label never refers to two objects, and failed attempts (E10) are generated so "tried to" is not a cue.

weaknesses.what: The question-phrasing bank is starved and that, not model capacity, is the single biggest data limit. After fallback fill, 13 of 22 question banks have exactly ONE train phrasing and one held-out phrasing (q.where_object, q.where_person, q.who_has, q.why_at, q.plan_get, q.next_to, q.where_before, q.where_at_time, q.rule_material, q.rule_category, q.rule_container, q.rule_place, q.yn_has). Teacher banks meanwhile have 46-95 train patterns each. The model is asked to map an unseen phrasing to the right answer space after one training example of that question type.
