open_questions: Is the Core-track held-out collapse a wording problem or a names/styles problem? Nothing currently separates them: all 3,763 held-out questions are simultaneously unseen wording, unseen style and fresh names. The cheapest decisive experiment is to regenerate held-out splits with the TRAIN question-phrasing bank held fixed (everything else unchanged) and re-score the same checkpoint — a few minutes of generation plus 5 s of eval.

How much of the 23% is simply one-phrasing-per-type? A second cheap run: top up the 13 starved q.* banks to 20+ accepted patterns with gen_patterns.py topup, regenerate, retrain 600 s. If Q6/Q8/Q11 recover, phrasing scarcity is the wall and no architecture change is indicated yet.

Should Q12 (plan) stay in the Step 1 gate? It is 12% of the held-out set, 0/448 held-out and 1/65 in-distribution, and it drags the headline number. Options: keep but report apart (as repeats already are), or give it explicit format supervision.

What corpus size should the medium preset be? At 24.15M tokens the 600 s run does 13.7 epochs; generation is 74 s per 20,000 visits, so 200,000 visits costs ~12 min. Is the 4M model data-limited or capacity-limited? A single run at 10x data with the same wall clock answers this and also un-confounds the 4M-vs-28M comparison.

Does the simulator need to get faster at all, or should the project simply accept pre-generated corpora? live_supply_ratio is 0.43, so the design's 5% live-generation requirement is currently unmet; it only matters if the sleep/self-tutoring phases of the vision need on-line world generation.

What is the intra-visit ICC for question correctness? Without it, none of the reported Wilson intervals (or the planned pool-control and H1 A/B comparisons) have honest width. This is a pure post-processing question — the per-item predictions with visit ids are already saved.

Should "not told" be rebalanced? UNTOLD_PICK=0.5 makes not-told-ness predictable from the question alone at 60.5% vs a 50% null, and not-told is 15.2% of the gate. Making the untold rate depend on the world rather than on the question type would close that leak.

Why does the person answer class leak through the answer line's wording (target_line 38.0% vs 18.3%)? Likely too few distinct phrasings for person-valued answers; worth checking whether the fix is more answer phrasings or a change in how the oracle renders person answers.

uncovered: No checker/verifier head exists anywhere in premonition/ (grep finds only learnlab's pattern-bank checker and village/oracle.py:875 check_plan), yet the hint ladder, effort drive, mastery drive, self-tutoring and REM dream-checking all assume one (design/03-issues-and-decisions.md:35 'agreed in principle'). Five vision mechanisms are blocked on a component no idea proposes building.

Plan questions (Q12) are 0/448 held-out and 1/65 in-distribution, 12% of the gate, with 0 right_exact and 0 right_other_working_plan out of 549 oracle-checked. The only recorded response is an OPEN question about dropping them from the gate; no idea proposes how a sequence-valued answer graded by simulation should be trained (format supervision, rejection sampling against the checker, or a separate head).

The village oracle can verify any plan by acting it out (learnlab/village/oracle.py:875; 549/549 plan questions oracle-checked) and computes a full symbolic derivation per question (Deriv: steps, evidence refs, rule families, oracle.py:102-117). Both are used only for scoring and for picking gold_lines. Nothing uses the oracle as a training signal, as an intermediate-step target, or at inference time - the single richest free supervision source in the project is idle.

The uncounted minGRU scan: premonition/flops.py:5-7 states elementwise work is skipped, and min_gru_scan (model.py:51-70) is a fp32 autocast-disabled chunked loop producing [B,T,d] intermediates twice per layer. The map raises this as an OPEN question and no idea measures it, so the equal-FLOPs budget may silently give D several times A's real seconds, which would void any 'D beats A at equal compute' conclusion - the project's headline claim.

The control arms are under-tuned and no idea strengthens them. Contender C's BM25 drops who/what/where/which/whose as stopwords (lookup.py:83-90) - exactly the question-type words - and stops its 192-token recall at the FIRST overlong line instead of skipping it (lookup.py:320-327); contender A has no answer-token weighting. Every headline comparison is D vs A/C, so a win may be a statement about weak baselines.

The slot binder (model.py:471-481) runs a Python loop over fetch slots using non-accumulating index_put, which is order-nondeterministic across cards that share an (owner, slot) pair (the `repeat` mask guards only within one card), and it is explicitly excluded from the FLOP hand count as '<1%' (flops.py:144) on a matmul-size estimate rather than a launch count. No idea covers either the correctness hazard or the cost.

NameOverflow (>16 distinct names in a visit) raises uncaught in data.py:406-409, aborting a whole cache build. Nothing addresses it, and it is a hard scale blocker for the 10x-data runs that several ideas depend on.

The 'not told' leak is generator-caused and no idea proposes the generator-side fix: scheduler.UNTOLD_PICK=0.5 makes not-told-ness predictable from the question alone at 60.5% against a 50% null (p_adj=2.1e-9), and 'not told' is 571/3763 = 15.2% of the gate. Same for the person/target_line leak at 38.0% vs an 18.3% null, which is a symptom of too few person-answer phrasings. The leak-panel-as-gate idea detects these; nothing fixes them.

The counterfactual-twin test fails for a supply reason no idea targets: n=210 usable linked twins out of 1,200 pair visits, 20 hits, p=0.048 against alpha=0.01. The cause is the low link yield in scheduler.counterfactual_pair (learnlab/village/scheduler.py:864-895), not item cost, so 'generate more items' does not straightforwardly fix it.

Live world generation runs at live_supply_ratio 0.43 against the design's 5%-of-learner-time requirement (269k tok/s world vs 633k tok/s learner). No idea decides whether on-line generation is actually needed for the sleep/self-tutoring/dream phases or whether the requirement should be formally retired in favour of pre-generated corpora.

A strength left unimproved: the pointerizer is exactly invertible and ENT ids not mentioned in the visible prefix are masked to -inf, so a fresh name is copied and can never be hallucinated (pointer.py:214-238, model.py:738-747). It covers person names only. Nothing proposes extending the same pointer discipline to objects, containers, places and times - which is precisely where the who-has-what / what-is-in-what binding and leak failures live.

The two tracks are never reconciled: no document says which is primary, and their tokenizer identities are incompatible (premonition-tok-v2.json, 7,289 ids, used by all three BensPC pilots vs the 7,068-id fallback required by premonition/identity.py), so identity.guard_verdict still returns full_verdict:false and no pilot checkpoint can be admitted for an official verdict. No idea addresses the reconciliation or the merge path.

Adversarial-review open problems #22-#25 (sleep-transaction versioning and re-keying of cards written during sleep; separate sleep-gating data plus an untouched shadow test; simulated lifetime budgets for diary bytes, active cards, code growth, retrieval cost and sleep FLOPs; a standalone drive-scheduler test) were logged on 18 Sep and never revisited by any memo or idea, while continual-sleep ideas assume them solved.

The told-ledger is adopted with no instantiated parameters: the scoring rule (+1 correct, 0 don't-know, -t/(1-t) wrong) has no value for t and no coverage floor, and its interaction with deliberate gist fading is unaddressed. The motivation memo's own five open questions are likewise unanswered and nothing depends on answering them.

Card age is an absolute 16-bucket log2 line distance with 8 buckets that never occur (store.py:100-116), and the map's own OPEN question asks whether relative rank within eligible cards would be better. No idea touches the recency signal, even though it is the store's ONLY ordering signal (no confidence, version, importance or source priority).

extra_lenses.focus:
TARGETS (blocking): every Premonition run is hardcoded to CPU - premonition/train.py:1013 and :1141 pass "cpu", scripts/premonition_ovn_retrieval.py:168 passes "cpu", the ladder inherits it, and autocast/fused-AdamW are gated on CUDA - so every seed, gate and curriculum conclusion in the project rests on 1,405-4,000-step CPU runs under a 30-minute ledger, on a machine that owns a 16 GB Blackwell RTX 5070 Ti that trains a 4M transformer at 0.5-0.65M tok/s. Also targets the major weakness that FlopCounterMode skips the minGRU scan (premonition/flops.py:5-7) while min_gru_scan (model.py:51-70) is a fp32 autocast-disabled chunked Python loop over logcumsumexp, so 'equal FLOPs' may hand D several times A's real seconds; and the blocking 'seed instability measured but not managed' (503/512 vs 27/512), which on a 16 GB card is a scheduling problem, not a compute problem - a 2M model is ~8 MB of weights.

SEARCH A (make the GPU usable): PyTorch on Blackwell / sm_120 (cu128 / cu129 wheel support, what silently falls back, TF32 and bf16 defaults, known Windows CUDA gotchas over SSH); torch.compile and CUDA graphs for models whose step time is dominated by kernel-launch overhead rather than arithmetic; GPU implementations of associative / chunked parallel scans (Heinsen associative scan, mamba/minGRU chunked scan kernels, whether a real-space cumulative-product formulation beats the log-space one in speed and stability, fp32 logcumsumexp memory traffic, chunk_size tuning); training many tiny models concurrently on one GPU (CUDA streams, torch.vmap / functorch model ensembling, 'parallel seed training', MPS service on Windows) so that 5-8 seeds per arm cost roughly one run; multi-seed and hyperparameter sweeps as first-class scheduling (ASHA / successive halving, Optuna or Ray Tune on a single GPU, median-of-seeds reporting); determinism and reproducibility flags on GPU vs CPU, and whether CPU-obtained rankings replicate on GPU at all.

SEARCH B (make 'equal compute' honest): iso-FLOP vs iso-wall-clock vs iso-parameter vs iso-data comparison protocols for non-transformer architectures; roofline / arithmetic-intensity and memory-bandwidth accounting for recurrent and state-space models; published critiques of FLOP-matched SSM-vs-transformer comparisons and of throughput claims that ignore elementwise work; 'strong baseline' / 'bag of tricks' / tuned-baseline reproducibility literature, i.e. how much a claimed architectural win shrinks once the baseline is tuned - directly relevant because contender C's BM25 drops who/what/where as stopwords and truncates its recall budget at the first overlong line, and contender A has no answer-token weighting. Wanted output: a concrete GPU run protocol (batch size, precision, compile, seeds-per-arm, what to log) plus a defensible definition of the efficiency axis the project claims to win on (accuracy per weight / per token / per second).

TARGETS (blocking): the corpus contains narration, teacher lines, questions and answers - and not one reasoning step. Answer tokens are 3.05% of train tokens (9,684 of 317,154) and carry the whole burden of a derivation the generator already knows: learnlab/village/oracle.py:102-117 builds a full symbolic Deriv per question (steps, the exact set of evidence refs, the rule families applied), and it is used ONLY to tag depth and to pick gold_lines. The measured consequences: Q11 why 28.8% -> 0.0%, Q8 rule 58.5% -> 4.0%, Q7 what-if 72.2% -> 7.2% held-out; Q12 plan 0/448; and in Premonition-mini the second fetch asks for a relation it practised in that position rather than the one the question names (0/171 held-out, 9/171 longer), with both required cards fetched 1/189. A written derivation names the second relation explicitly, turning a latent credit-assignment problem into token-level supervision - and it needs no oracle EVIDENCE LABELS at the store level, which is the map's own 'cheapest missing signal' OPEN question.

SEARCH: chain-of-thought and rationale distillation into sub-100M models - 'Distilling step-by-step', 'Specializing smaller language models towards multi-step reasoning', Orca-style explanation tuning, TinyGSM, and crucially the NEGATIVE results on the size below which CoT supervision fails to transfer or hurts; scratchpad / 'show your work' intermediate-computation supervision and its length-generalisation behaviour; program-of-thought and executable-trace supervision where a symbolic solver writes the trace (exactly this project's situation); process supervision vs outcome supervision at small scale; knowledge distillation for tiny LMs (sequence-level KD, logit/dark-knowledge KD, teacher-forced trace vs sampled trace) - Qwen already runs locally and already wrote the pattern bank, so it is available as a teacher over the same village text; 'textbook-quality' / phi-style data rewriting and multi-rendering of the same fact; and the question of whether a trace at inference time is needed at all or whether trace-only-at-training ('implicit CoT', internalised CoT, CoT compression into latent steps) works at 4M - which also connects directly to the unbuilt latent-thought stage. Wanted output: whether to render oracle derivations as text, how long, at what mixing ratio, whether the model should emit them at test time, and the measured cost-benefit against simply upweighting answer tokens.

TARGETS: the project has an exact, cheap, deterministic verifier - the village oracle grades a plan by acting it out (learnlab/village/oracle.py:875; whole final eval 5.46 s) - and it has NO checker head anywhere in premonition/, although the hint ladder, effort drive, mastery drive, self-tutoring and REM dream-checking all assume one (design/03:35 'agreed in principle'). It also has three failures that verification-and-search answers directly: choosing among distractor cards sits at 166-182/512, BELOW a measured 53.71% question-blind shortcut floor, so the reasoner may currently be worse than not reasoning; held-out two-hop composition is 14/189 with a single greedy retrieval path per question; Q12 plan questions are 0/448 despite being checkable by simulation; and the HALT head is trained on teacher-forced correctness, used on free-running greedy decoding at weight 0.1, and scores 525/1024 at 2.74 loops - barely above chance.

SEARCH: verifier training and generator-verifier gaps at small scale ('Training verifiers to solve math word problems' and its successors, how best-of-n scales with n for models under 100M, when best-of-n plateaus or starts rewarding hacks); outcome reward models vs process reward models, and whether a PRM is affordable when the process labels are free from a simulator; self-consistency / majority vote over SAMPLED retrieval paths rather than greedy top-k (directly aimed at the second-fetch-wrong-relation failure: sample k ASK chains, keep the one whose fetched facts actually support an answer the checker accepts); STaR / rejection-sampling fine-tuning / RFT - sample k plans, keep the ones the simulator says work, train on those (the obvious untried fix for Q12 0/448); reranking of multi-hop retrieval chains and chain-level scoring in multi-hop QA; selective prediction, abstention and confidence calibration for tiny models as a principled replacement for the HALT head (ponder cost, entropy-based exit, calibration under distribution shift); test-time compute scaling results from 2025-26 on small models, including the negative ones (where extra sampling buys nothing because the model's top-k never contains the right answer). Wanted output: whether a ~50-100k-param checker head trained against the oracle is affordable inside the 2M budget, whether verification should be a training signal, an inference-time search, or both, and what shortcut floor any verified arm must clear before it counts.

TARGETS: Premonition-mini is, mechanically, a 2015-2018 memory-augmented network rebuilt from scratch - soft cosine addressing over key/value slots, multi-hop queries, a recurrent controller with a learned halt, per-entity gated slots, FIFO eviction - and its current symptoms are that era's documented failure modes almost one for one. That literature is the cheapest available source of BOTH fixes to copy and dead ends to skip, and no existing lens mines it systematically (neuro-inspired looks at brains; slots-pointers looks at modern slot attention). The map itself already quotes one instance without following it up: 'End-To-End Memory Networks needed a linear start, noise and best-of-10 restarts for the same reason' - i.e. the published recipe for exactly the 503/512-vs-27/512 seed lottery where two seeds land on opposite pooling solutions.

SEARCH: End-to-End Memory Networks (the linear-start / injected-noise / best-of-10-restarts training recipe, and the reported variance across restarts); Key-Value Memory Networks (separate key and value encodings of the SAME item - literally the untrained two-pool fix, plus what their key-addressing/value-reading split bought); Dynamic Memory Networks and DMN+ (episodic memory with multiple passes, per-hop attention gates and per-hop supervision - the order-free-set-loss problem); Recurrent Entity Networks (independent gated memory slots with per-key write gates - the fix for a binder that writes one pooled value into every entity slot a line mentions); Relation Networks and their accuracy-per-parameter on relational one- and two-hop questions (a direct efficiency benchmark for a 2M reasoner); Neural Turing Machines, DNC and Sparse Access Memory (usage-based allocation, temporal link matrices for recall ORDER, and the reproducibility reports on how brittle they were) - aimed at permanent eviction, at 'fetched' doubling as an eviction mask, and at hop ordering; Universal Transformer plus Adaptive Computation Time and the published evidence that ACT halting usually learns nothing without careful ponder-cost tuning - the HALT diagnosis; and bAbI's own history: which tasks were solved, which were shown to be leaky or saturated, what the standard 10k-vs-1k and multi-restart protocol was, and the post-mortems on why memory-augmented networks lost to plain transformers (was it capability, optimisation brittleness, or just scale?). Wanted output: a short list of mechanisms to copy verbatim, a short list of mechanisms with published evidence they do not work under backprop at this scale, and an honest statement of what the plain-transformer contender is expected to give up.

dropped.title: MUVERA-style structured card keys: a fixed-size key that approximates token-level matching, with no learned pool to collapse
dropped.reason: The citations are fine - MUVERA 2405.19504 (NeurIPS 2024) is accurately described, including asymmetric fixed dimensional encodings as the first single-vector proxy for multi-vector similarity with theoretical guarantees, 2-5x fewer candidates, 10% improved recall and 90% lower latency on BEIR; 2510.06182 and 2510.06477 also check out; 2410.22669 exists as Hadamard-derived linear Binding (HLB), though its 'exact unbinding' is not confirmed by the abstract. The idea is dropped on fit and feasibility, not on sources. (a) It aims at the wrong failure. The measured second-hop failure is that the query REQUESTS the wrong relation (held-out requested-relation selection 0/171 default, 9/171 longer; 00-evidence.md), and the project's own diagnosis is 'no factorised query construction - the model learned position-specific relation priors'. A better-shaped KEY cannot fix a query that names the wrong relation; it will retrieve the wrong card more accurately. (b) The dissociation is already measured: in m02, recall@4 was 1.0 - the right card was always fetched - while accuracy stayed at 60/1024 validation and 54/1024 test. Addressing has already been shown not to be the binding constraint in that regime. (c) The dimensions are hopeless. MUVERA's FDEs are thousands of dimensions; Premonition's key_dim is 64 at production width and 16 on the toy the test would run on (config.py:105-106; scripts/premonition_ovn_ladder.py:234). Eight buckets of 8 dims is already far outside the regime where the epsilon bound means anything; eight buckets of 2 dims on the toy is meaningless. (d) The 'two-part question naturally lights up two buckets' claim does not hold in this architecture: the ASK query is heads.query(register) from register 0 (model.py:492-496), a learned projection of a think register, not a bag of question token states. Making it an FDE over question tokens is a rewrite of the query path, not a drop-in key swap, and that rewrite is already on the project's list as the deferred 'compositional hop-2 query built from the fetched link card's entity pointer plus the question's relation'. (e) The project rejected ColBERT-style addressing twice; MUVERA answers the COST objection, but cost was never the only objection - the standing reason is 'defer until a correctly formed query has an addressing failure', and that condition is still unmet.

dropped.title: Stop fresh-name embeddings from collapsing: freeze or periodically reset the name-syllable embeddings in the Core track
dropped.reason: The citations are genuine and accurately described - arXiv 2604.21632 confirms 10-layer 60-75M transformers near 0% on unseen predicates, the embedding-collapse diagnosis with an l2-regularised-GD proof, and the fixes (copy attention, vocabulary diversity 9,600 vs 150/600/2,400, frozen embeddings, reinitialisation every 100-1,000 steps, ~90% combined, plus the Gemma 3 unused-token evidence); arXiv 2307.01163 confirms active forgetting resets the embedding layer every K updates, helps language adaptation and wins in the low-data regime for distant languages. The idea nevertheless fails on fit, twice over, and both failures are decisive. FIRST, THE TARGET NUMBER IS DEAD. The 0.0% fresh-name result in the four artifacts/premonition-1h-4090-run_*.log runs is an already-diagnosed tokenizer bug, written up in design/research/2026-09-18-fresh-names.md:7 and design/research/2026-09-18-decisions-log.md:16: those runs loaded premonition-tok-v1-fallback.json, which has no syllable list, so the name-splitting rule never ran, 262 train names were single tokens and no held-out name was. Those checkpoints are formally refused as primary evidence (design/06-premonition-mini-spec.md:282). SECOND, THE MECHANISM CANNOT APPLY. data/tokenizer/premonition-tok-v2.json contains 24 two-letter name syllables (ba, da, fe, gi, ho, ju, ke, ku, li, lo, mi, mo, ne, nu, pa, ra, re, sa, si, ta, to, ve, vi, zo) and every name in every split is built from them, so there are no rare or unseen name tokens whose embeddings could contract - the artifact's own audit shows 0 single-token names in all three splits and a mean-pieces gap of 0.0026. A fresh name is a novel COMBINATION of highly frequent, well-trained syllables. The 'To See the Unseen' failure is about tokens the model rarely or never predicts; freezing frequent syllable rows attacks nothing, and 'active forgetting' here would be a generic plasticity intervention aimed at a non-existent problem.

dropped.title: Make cards re-fetchable and keep two hop-1 hypotheses alive (a beam of width 2 over the first fetch)
dropped.reason: The eviction half - which is the whole 'possibly free' argument and the reason the idea is ranked cheap - is already answered in the saved artifacts, and the answer is no. Every logged value of the project's own counters is zero: 13 records of fifo_overflow_questions: 0 and 13 of fifo_gold_evicted_questions: 0 across artifacts/opus-m02-20260918-232457 (own-bypass.log and runs/own-D-card-bypass-v16-s0-1000.json). That is consistent with the measured halting behaviour - learned halting averages 2.7412 loops at test, so top_k 4 inserts roughly 11 cards into 16 rows and the ring never wraps. The proposal's own step-zero screen therefore resolves against it before any run, and the project OPEN question it cites ('has any run logged eviction counts?') is already closed. With eviction absent, no part of the 1/189 both-facts-fetched number is a bookkeeping artefact, so the headline claim of the idea does not hold. The code reading itself is correct - I confirmed store.py's `ok &= ~fetched` and model.py's `position = _card_base + (count + order) % card_rows` never reconcile - but it is a latent bug with no measured consequence at current loop counts, not a blocking failure. Citations are also the weakest of the batch: Beam Retrieval and Baleen are real papers, but the two claims the idea leans on ('beam size 2 is the best accuracy/compute balance', Baleen 'complements greedy search in improving recall considerably' and 96.3% recall@20) are search-result paraphrases I could not confirm in either abstract.

dropped.title: Add a contiguity buffer: every fetched card silently drags in its temporal neighbours
dropped.reason: The citations are the cleanest of the eight, and the mechanism is genuinely new to the project's list (the age bias at store.py:100-116 is card age, not neighbourhood). But the premise — 'the two facts a two-hop question needs were usually narrated close together' — is false for the dataset the target number comes from, and this is checkable by reading premonition/toy_ladder.py rather than by running anything. The proposal's own step 0 would discover this, but it can be discovered for free right now, which removes the reason to spend an arm on it. It also collides with the 16-row FIFO it would consume, and the idea itself concedes it could act as a shortcut that makes the model look right without composing — a bad property for the project's headline reasoning claim. Drop as an arm. The only part worth keeping is the 30-second line-distance count on village v0 (not the ladder), where gold evidence placement is scheduler-driven and genuinely unknown; if that median turns out to be 1-2 lines, the idea can be resurrected against Core-track data.

dropped.title: Evidence depletion instead of a permanent fetched-mask, plus clearing `fetched` when a card row is recycled
dropped.reason: The eviction bug is real in code but cannot be implicated in any measured failure, and the proposed decisive test is guaranteed to return zero by construction. premonition_ovn_retrieval.py:10 fixes max_loops = 4 for every arm, and the bypass-k1 arm that produced every quoted retrieval number uses top_k = 1 (ARMS at line 31). That is at most 3 fetches into 16 card rows. Even bypass-k4 would be 12 into 16. So the 1/189 both-facts-fetched result, the 0-9/171 wrong-relation result and the 14/189 held-out two-hop result were all produced under a configuration where FIFO wrap is impossible, and 'log eviction counts against the held-out two-hop failures on an existing checkpoint' will report zero without telling anyone anything. The idea also concedes, correctly, that it does not touch the diagnosed cause of the wrong-relation fetch (one 64-d query from one register with no separate person and relation fields, model.py:492-496), and that clearing `fetched` alone may make the model re-fetch the same card every loop because set-CE gives it no reason to move on. The soft-depletion half rests on a paper (2605.02323, 'When Attention Collapses: Residual Evidence Modeling for Compositional Inference', Niklas Houba) which does exist but whose quantitative results neither the proposer nor I could extract, and whose benchmarks (LISA, FUSS) are vision/audio separation. Both halves of the idea are therefore weakly motivated for this project right now.

dropped.title: Promote the variant/read_only discipline into a declarative intervention harness (one-line patches instead of one-off subclasses)
dropped.reason: Dropped on fit, not on merit — it is competent engineering advice that happens not to be aimed at a measured weakness. It produces no result, its own risks section concedes it 'competes for the same hours as an actual experiment', and the project's standing guidance (and Ben's stated preference for minimal, targeted work) is to prefer cheap decisive tests. The specific blockage it claims to relieve does not hold up: the OPEN question it names — append the card's key and source tag to the row and re-run supplied-card choosing — is a ~20-line subclass in the existing, already-audited variant style (card_pools.py's fork_rng + from_base pattern), which is far less work than a site registry plus an Intervention spec plus no-op bit-identity assertions. And the flagship demonstration it picks is the one target the proposed mechanism provably cannot hit. If any part survives, it is the two-line version: write the card-row-format subclass now and skip the framework. Note this is the one idea in the batch whose target_part is a STRENGTH rather than a measured weakness, which is the tell.

dropped.title: Ask the decoder what a card says: a Patchscopes-style readout that tests usability, not decodability
dropped.reason: Dropped as a duplicate of results the project already holds. The proposal's stated payoff is: 'if a supplied single card reads out perfectly but choosing among four fails, the problem is selection, not representation'. That is already ESTABLISHED evidence — artifacts/opus-m02-20260918-232457/SUMMARY.txt:22-27 records D-card-bypass and D-think-gated at 1024/1024 on the untouched test at both seeds with one supplied card, and SUMMARY.txt:50-53 records the collapse as distractors are added (1024/674/545/444), with distractor values emitted 146-318 times. m03 reproduces it (answer-original-s0 read1 512/512 vs choose1 164/512). Reading a single supplied card by this decoder is perfect; choosing is what fails; that conclusion is four-for-four across fixes and seeds. The one piece the proposal adds — running the readout on pre-Think versus post-Think rows to measure what Think destroys — is also already measured in m02: nothink writer-card 477/512 versus 55/512 with one Think pass, cos_post 0.9756 versus 0.2362, card-row attention 0.0774 versus 0.3291. Combined with a mechanism that cannot produce its own headline number on this data, nothing is left. If the underlying question is still live, idea 2 answers it causally and idea 4 answers the selection half exactly.

dropped.title: Learning-progress bandit over question types and phrasings, instead of a fixed question mix
dropped.reason: The citations are the best-supported in this batch: SEC (2505.14970) is exactly a non-stationary bandit per problem category with absolute advantage as learning-gain proxy and TD(0) updates, reporting better OOD generalisation and skill balance; the noisy-TV paper (2509.25438, ICLR 2026) does prove learning progress is a monotone indicator of information gain via an error model. The idea nevertheless fails on fit, arithmetic and feasibility. FIT: the measured held-out collapse (Q6 62.4%->1.1%, Q8 58.5%->4.0%, Q11 28.8%->0.0%) is question-type IDENTIFICATION from unseen wording, with 13 of 22 q.* banks holding exactly one train phrasing - and 'held-out' wording for those 13 is one of Ben's own fallback seeds. A curriculum reweights how often a type is practised; it cannot invent a phrasing, and the proposer concedes this. So the mechanism does not touch the diagnosed cause. ARITHMETIC: the claimed budget saving does not exist. Q12 is 6.9% of train QUESTIONS, and answer tokens are 3.05% of all tokens (9,684 of 317,154 on shard 0), so Q12 answers are roughly 0.2% of the training token budget. Reweighting away from Q12 recovers about one fifth of one percent of compute, because the model still trains on the whole narrated visit either way. The claimed '~7% of train questions currently returning nothing' is true and irrelevant to compute. FEASIBILITY: the reward is not free. Per-type accuracy is computed in the final scoring path (learnlab/step1.py:1580 by_qtype) and at eval segments (step1.py:2200), not online per arm; and the corpus is pregenerated (artifact world.pregenerated = true) with live_supply_ratio 0.43, so changing the mix online means regenerating shards or importance-resampling whole visits - questions are embedded inside narrated visits, so the type mix cannot be changed without re-running the generator. That is not 'the bandit's reward is free'. Finally the project's own open question already names the decisive, cheaper experiment: top up the 13 starved q.* banks with gen_patterns.py and re-run 600 s. Do that first; if phrasing scarcity is the wall, the curriculum question is moot.

dropped.title: A standing partial-input shortcut panel for the Premonition toy, scored in the same cells as the model
dropped.reason: The premise is false. A systematic partial-input panel already exists in the Premonition toy: scripts/premonition_ovn_ladder.py:168 `shortcut_ceilings()` scores SEVEN rules that each ignore part of the question, in TWO cells (one_hop and two_hop), and the result is written into exp1/data/manifest.json. I read the stored values: one_hop {entity_match_any_relation 0.5371, relation_match_any_entity 0.5332, random_attribute_card 0.3037, entity_not_in_question 0.0703, object_of_any_link 0.0, relation_match_and_object_of_a_link... 0.0, relation_match_and_entity_not_a_link_object 0.5332} and a matching two_hop block. So 53.71% is one of fourteen numbers, not 'a single unpaired 53.7%', and the project already reports the 166-182/512 scores against it in 00-evidence.md. Worse for the proposal's risk section: the ~50% ceiling is DESIGNED IN, not an artifact to be fixed. premonition/toy_ladder.py's docstring states that distractors deliberately mirror the evidence and that 'Any rule that ignores the question's person ... scores at most about 50%'. Fixing the generator, as the risks suggest, would destroy the diagnostic. What remains genuinely missing is thin: the ceilings are computed on validation while the headline choosing numbers are on test, and there is no TRAINED question-only baseline (all seven existing rules are analytic). Those are a few lines inside the existing function, not a new panel — fold them into idea 4 or idea 1 rather than running this as its own item.

dropped.title: Write cards with a vector-symbolic bind instead of a learned pool (HLB/HRR role-filler card format)
dropped.reason: Citations largely hold: arXiv 2410.22669 is real (Alam, Oberle, Raff, Biderman, Oates, Holt; NeurIPS 2024) and the abstract does say HLB is built for computational efficiency, classic VSA tasks and differentiable systems. 2111.06077 is a real ACM Computing Surveys HDC/VSA Part I survey, but its abstract lists TPR/HRR/MAP/BSC/SBDR and does NOT explicitly state the Hadamard-product or FHRR-complex-multiply details the proposer attributes to it. 2505.06191 (Mao, Tenenbaum, Wu, May 2025) is real and does claim data efficiency, compositional generalisation, continual learning and zero-shot transfer. The idea is dropped on FIT and NOVELTY, not on citations. The project has already run a strictly STRONGER version of this experiment and it failed. premonition/direct_reader.py (milestone-3 continuation, decisions log 'Astra review of milestone 3 and the direct-reader continuation') removes pooling entirely: every token position of a selected line enters the decoder as its own row, so the decoder's question-conditioned cross-attention sees the uncompressed reader states, which already decode person and value at 2304/2304. That is the perfect-card-format upper bound this idea asks for. Measured result, validation, direct vs pooled: reading 512 vs 512 (s0), 512 vs 485 (s1); choosing 170 vs 164 (s0), 162 vs 161 (s1). The predeclared choosing rule was INCONCLUSIVE and the test split agreed. So identity/content competition in the pool is NOT what caps choosing, and the idea's falsifiable intermediate signal (both fields decodable from one card) is already satisfied with no accuracy movement. The same continuation found 'Relevant-pair both-correct is 0/256 in every arm' and 'relevant swaps change the prediction in only 2-9 of 256 triplets, so the answers follow the SET of card values, not their binding to a person and relation' - a binding-format fix cannot repair an answer path that is not using binding at all. This is the fourth card-writer repair after original, mean-pool and two-pool (decisions log m03: mean pool 512/164 -> 363/138 seed 0, 485/161 -> 316/125 seed 1; two-pool fetched gold LESS often and 'the value pool did not specialise').

dropped.title: Dendritic context gating for the entity binder, so subject, object and value slots stop receiving identical content
dropped.reason: The citation is exactly right (Iyer, Grewal, Velu, Souza, Forest, Ahmad 2022; f(m,n) = m*sigmoid(n) with k-WTA; MT10 87.5% vs 76.6%; permutedMNIST 94.6%/81.4%; prototype-based context so no task ID at inference). The proposal itself does not work as specified. The binder ALREADY computes a per-slot multiplicative gate from [slot; value]: bind() is sigmoid(gate)*(tanh(content) - slot) with gate,content = W_b[s;v] (premonition/model.py:242-245). The proposed role branches score the CARD VALUE, which is identical for every entity slot that card binds into (model.py:471-481 expands value[:, k] over all ents of the card), so the winning branch and therefore sigmoid(winner) is the same for all of that line's slots -- it cannot distinguish subject from object by construction. The context channel would have to depend on the (slot, card) pair or on the entity's position within the line, which the idea does not propose. Combined with the fact that active-dendrite gains come from multi-task continual learning rather than intra-episode syntactic roles, and with only 16 slots and <=4 entities per line, expected upside is very low.

dropped.title: Neuromodulatory row gating: freeze fetched evidence rows in Think and recycle the fetched mask with the FIFO
dropped.reason: Both halves fail against the code. (1) The eviction hypothesis is arithmetically impossible for the number it claims to explain: the 1/189 both-facts-fetched result comes from arm bypass-k1, which is configured top_k=1 with MAX_LOOPS=4 (scripts/premonition_ovn_retrieval.py:10, 31), and own_fixed does at most loops-1 = 3 fetch rounds, so at most 3 cards ever enter 16 rows. No card was evicted in any measured exp2 run, and fifo_overflow_questions would be 0. (2) The 'freeze fetched evidence rows' half is already adopted and already in force for that very number: D-card-bypass keeps the pre-Think rows for the decoder (premonition/answer_path.py:10-13, 114-121) and every exp2 arm quoted is a bypass arm. The gating citation (arXiv 2512.13859) is verified, but it is about which units may update in a Hopfield attractor, and the eLife read-mode/write-mode framing attributed to it here is not something I could confirm. Net: one half duplicates an adopted decision, the other half addresses a failure mode that has never occurred.

dropped.title: BTSP-style eligibility-trace card writing: bind a whole line by one instructive pulse, not by a competitive softmax
dropped.reason: The Nature Communications BTSP paper is real (Wu & Maass, 'A simple model for Behavioral Time Scale Synaptic Plasticity (BTSP) provides content addressable memory with binary synapses and one-shot learning', published 2 January 2025, 16:342, not 2024) and does support content-addressable memory with binary synapses and one-shot learning; the other two BTSP sources remain unopened by both of us. But this is the fourth member of a family whose first three members have now been measured and failed: original, uniform mean (512->363 reading, no choosing gain) and two-pool (fetched gold less often, value pool did not specialise), all in m03. An exponential eligibility trace read out at the line's end token is a decay-weighted fixed pooling function, i.e. the already-listed [conditional] 'fixed position-sensitive pooling (MemN2N positional encoding)' from final-sweep 04-efficiency proposal 1 with one extra hyperparameter. The proposer's own risk section concedes both points. The BTSP literature's saturating one-shot rule is also explicitly poor at extracting regularities over thousands of repetitions, which is the regime here.
